analyst_view.overall: Kairat (27th of 36, two points from three games) host Mjällby (9th, seven points) in Almaty on matchday 4 and need a win to climb out of the elimination places after a 1-1 draw at Atalanta, under interim coach Zhora Harutyunyan, who took over when Rafael Urazbakhtin left in late October. Kairat's domestic season is over, so they come in with about three weeks without a competitive game, and their weak recent shooting and leaky defence (14 conceded in six, including 1-5 at home to Panathinaikos) are already in the numbers. Mjällby flew out on Monday via Istanbul (around nine hours in the air each way) and still have an Allsvenskan finale at Halmstad to come, where points matter after a season spent near the bottom; forward Jacob Bergström went off after 41 minutes against Malmö with a thigh problem and his place in the trip was still described as uncertain, while Dalsgaard and Stavitski (already in the numbers) stay out. Polish referee Paweł Raczkowski has now been named; his low card record (3.8 a game) is already in the numbers, so the view still leans only slightly lower on shooting.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already trim Kairat for scoring only 3 in their last six. Kairat's long break could blunt their attack but also loosen a defence that let in five at home to Panathinaikos, while a missing Bergström or a rotated Mjällby side after the long trip points slightly down, so with these pulling both ways I stay at 2.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners, already cutting Kairat for winning only 12 in their last six and lifting Mjällby a little for their recent 17 in three. Kairat will want to push at home, but Mjällby as the fresher, in-season side can keep the ball, which the near-even split (4.4 to 4.3) already shows, so I stay at 8.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, already taking a little off for referee Paweł Raczkowski (3.8 cards a game in his six games on record) and for Mjällby's tidy recent record. There is no rivalry between the clubs; a Kairat side that must win could foul more if they fall behind, but that is a hunch, so I stay at 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots and already take about 7% off Kairat for their low recent shooting. I trim a little more, to about 24.2, because Kairat have had no competitive game for around three weeks under an interim coach, and Mjällby may be without Bergström after his thigh injury and could rotate after the long trip with a league finale to come; the numbers can't see either.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, already cutting Kairat by about 10% for only 14 on target in six and lifting Mjällby for their accurate recent shooting. Kairat's lack of match rhythm since their league season ended and the doubt over Bergström, Mjällby's main aerial threat, point a little lower, so I go to about 8.1.
